label: late copy-phase steps fed back a token from a favoured set (o, j, m, i, t, r, ...)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, never during the original tokens or at <DEL>, and never on the first two outputs (recall_idx 0 or 1). It also never fires on the first occurrence of a token (in_first=0 is always true when active). Within the copy phase the rate climbs toward the end: to_go 0-1 holds about 75% of the activation mass, and nothing fires with to_go >= 6. The input token, which is the model's own fed-back previous output, strongly modulates the rate: o (23%), j, m, i, t and r (11-16%) are well above other tokens. The strongest activations come from L=3 sequences at the final step (t=5) with o, t, m, j or 3 as input. Copy-phase position alone has recall 1.0 but precision only 0.15. Adding to_go<=2 and the token set gets dev F1 about 0.51 (P 0.42, R 0.66, mass recall 0.71). The rest of the token dependence is graded and was not captured by any clean rule.
